question: A Cisco MDS 9000 Series Switch is configured for SAN Analytics and SAN Telemetry Streaming. An engineer must enable analytics for NVMe on interfaces in the range of fc1/1-12. Due to a large amount of traffic generated in the SAN environment, the data must be collected at regular intervals of 60 seconds from ports fc1/1-12 and then for ports fc1/13-24 for the next 60 seconds. Ports in the range fc1/13-24 were already enabled for analytics. Which set of commands must be used to meet these requirements?
options:
analytics port-sampling module 1 size 12 interval 60000

interface fc1/1-12
  analytics fc-scsi
  analytics fc-nvme

analytics port-sampling module 1 size 12 interval 60

interface fc1/1-12
  analytics type fc-nvme

interface fc1/1-12
  port-sampling module 1 size 12 interval 60
  analytics nvme

interface fc1/1-12
  port-sampling module 1 size 12 interval 60000
  analytics type fc-scsi
theory: SAN Analytics on the MDS collects per-flow SCSI/NVMe metrics directly in hardware; you enable it per protocol on an interface with 'analytics type fc-nvme' (or fc-scsi), which is independent from the port-sampling feature used by SAN Telemetry Streaming to periodically push that data out. Because ports fc1/13-24 are already enabled and only need a new 60-second collection window, and fc1/1-12 needs both analytics enabled and sampling, the correct sequence enables NVMe analytics on the new range and lets the existing port-sampling group (interval expressed in milliseconds, so 60 seconds = 60000) apply. Mixing up seconds vs. milliseconds, or using a 'port-sampling' or 'nvme' keyword that doesn't exist under the interface, is the trap in the distractors. (Cisco MDS 9000 SAN Analytics and SAN Telemetry Streaming Configuration Guide)
